The Router marked 'Uniform brownish-orange... with no black points' as FALSE due to the white blaze. While technically the coat is not 'uniform' (solid) because of the white marking, in equine taxonomy, a Sorrel is defined by the absence of *black* points. White markings (blaze, socks) are common and do not disqualify the horse from being a Sorrel. However, strictly adhering to the checkpoint text 'Uniform... coloration', the presence of a large white patch makes it non-uniform. I agree with the Router's strict textual interpretation, but note that this is a semantic mismatch rather than a biological error. The horse IS a Sorrel. All other anatomical checkpoints (head, neck, legs, build) are correctly marked as present and testable.
